EPOL 590 · AI and Academic Literature · Lecture 3

Literature Workbench

Read an article closely, follow the literature around it, and map the field it belongs to — noticing, at each step, what AI changes.

What this is for

Tonight you will read one article closely, follow the literature around it, and map the field it belongs to. The point is not to produce summaries faster. It is to notice how scholarly arguments are built, what different traditions count as evidence, and whether AI preserves those differences or flattens them into a generic template.

The workbench is a scratchpad for that work. It keeps your reading notes, your discovery log and your map side by side, so you can see how a reading turns into a search and a search into a map. Your group's Google Doc remains the shared record: copy into it from here.

Seed articles

Group A · humanities / critical studies. Smart et al. (2026), “Toward a Theory of Value in AI Alignment,” arXiv:2608.10327 (preprint). The authors annotated 94 alignment papers to recover their theory of value. Article

Group B · science. Sharma et al. (2024), “Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models,” ICLR 2024. Read the main paper; the appendices are optional. Article

Both are open access under CC BY 4.0, so you may download them, share them and upload them to AI tools. Check the licence of anything else before uploading it.

Hour 1 · 5:15–6:20

1 · Read

Read your group's article by one strategy — sequential, overview-first or investigative — without AI first. Record the claim, warrant, uncertainty and your path. Then ask AI to follow the same route and record what changed. Finish with a handover brief.

Hour 2 · 6:30–7:15

2 · Search

Take the other group's article and brief. Trace its literature backward, forward and sideways, first conventionally and then with AI. Verify every reference before you log it as verified. No gap-hunting yet.

Hour 3 · 7:15–7:50

3 · Map

Map your original article's field, then look at it three ways: conceptual, chronological and relational. Exchange maps, critique, revise — and save each version with your reason for changing it.

Ground rules

  • Human first. Read before you prompt.
  • AI follows your route. Ask it to read the way you read, then compare.
  • Every citation is a lead, not a source, until you have found it and checked it says what is claimed.
  • A gap in the map may be a gap in your search or in how you drew it, not in the field.

Your data

Everything stays in this browser. Nothing is uploaded to Machine Spirits, and the workbench never calls an AI service — use a permitted tool such as NotebookLM or Gemini alongside it.

Reading record

Prompt for your strategy

Compare reading records

Which disagreement comes from the article, and which from where we entered it? Did AI preserve or flatten the discipline's standards of evidence?

6:15–6:20

Handover brief

For the group that searches outward from your article after the break.

Hour 2 · 6:30–7:15

2 · Search

Start from the other group's brief. Follow references backward, citing work forward, and dissenting or adjacent work sideways — conventionally first, then with AI. An AI-suggested reference is unverified until you have found it and read enough to confirm it says what is claimed.

3 · Map

Map your original article's field using your reading and the other group's discoveries. Then change the view: each one foregrounds something different and hides something else. Before calling an empty region a gap in the field, ask whether it is a gap in your search or in your drawing.
